# Ball carrier - design notes (generated by ball_carrier.py)

Payload: 30 x 40 mm balls = 81 g. Printed parts: 161 g (at 100 %, thin walls print solid). Robot estimate: 110 g. Total 352 g.

## Capacity
Balls dropped one by one into the lowest free spot (gravity tilted 8 deg): 32 fit inside the closed 115 mm tall box, so 30 have margin. Inside: 197 x 140 mm.

## Stability and traction
CG of robot + full box: x = 72 mm (drive axle at 0), z = 93 mm.
Load on the drive wheels: 50 % (front skid at x = 144).
Side tip-over at a_lat = 0.54 g -> max 0.89 m/s on a 150 mm radius curve, 1.26 m/s on 300 mm.

## Discharge
The whole front (140 x 115 mm = 3.5 D wide) swings away, so no arch can form (arching needs a roofed outlet narrower than ~4-5 D).
Floor 8 deg on 2 mm rails: a ball's rolling resistance is < 1 deg, so every ball rolls out.

## Latch: ratchet disc + gravity pawl
Ball bed on the gate (Rankine K = 0.41, bulk density 48 kg/m3, fill 111 mm): 6 N.mm static; with down-slope weight and 0.5 g braking 27 N.mm.
Force on the notch face (r = 6.4 mm): 0.86 N static, 4.18 N design. Its line passes 0.6 mm above the pawl pivot, so the load presses the tooth deeper (self-locking).
Release force at the paddle (tooth friction mu = 0.3 + locking moment, paddle arm 20 mm): 0.17-0.81 N; robot push at stall ~5.8 N -> 7x margin.
Release stroke: the pawl turns 11 deg = ~5 mm at the paddle; it sticks out 16 mm ahead of the arm tips.
Pawl CG is 5.2 mm behind and 5.7 mm below the pivot: gravity holds the tooth up and re-arms it; a forward jerk would need 0.9 g to lift it (unloaded).

## Reset
Push either side lever down (or lift the gate): the shaft turns the gate shut, the notch comes round under the tooth and the counterweighted pawl drops in - click, armed. Lever up = dumped.

## Shell and aerodynamics
Plain closed box, 0.8 mm skin, solid sides (the hinge shaft runs across the front, outside the box). Ball pressure on the walls is only ~K.rho.g.h = 21 Pa.
Drag at 1.5 m/s, frontal area 163 cm2: 0.023 N (box, Cd ~1.05) - 0.4 % of the drive force. Mass and CG height matter far more for speed.

## Printing (no supports)
Tray floor down, lid roof down, gate inner face down, disc / levers / pawl / latch cheeks flat, shaft and pins lying / standing, frames flat. Lid drops onto 4 corner tabs inside the tray.

## Assumptions (change at the top of ball_carrier.py)
Balls 40 mm / 2.7 g; tower rim 50 mm with an opening wider than 140 mm; chassis underside 22 mm above the floor.
